title: What Is an LLM?
summary: A large language model is a next-token predictor trained on a huge amount of text. Five short, animated tours: what it does, where it came from, what is inside, how it is made, and where it falls short.
objectives: Describe an LLM as a model that repeatedly predicts the next token, and read its output as probabilities
Place the transformer, GPT-3 and ChatGPT on the path from n-gram statistics to today's assistants
Name the stages inside a transformer (tokens, embeddings, attention and MLP blocks, softmax) and the stages that make an assistant (pretraining, fine-tuning, preference tuning)
Tell which tasks a plain LLM does well and which need tools or grounding
